name: Ugro Capital Ltd
title: Ugro Capital Ltd - 511742 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Ugro is shrinking its high-volume prime DSA book (~15-20% run-down a year) to swap into higher-yield branch LAP and embedded finance; AUM flat, opex cut to INR 490-500 cr, FY27 a transition year with no ROA guidance.

summary.headline: UGRO Capital says Q4 FY26 net total income rose 51% YoY to a figure not stated in the call, with GNPA at 2.5%, cost of borrowings at 10.16%, and FY27 opex guided to INR 490-500 crores.
summary.overview: UGRO Capital's first full quarter of its February 2026 structural realignment saw AUM broadly flat QoQ as the non-focus intermediated (DSA-led Prime) book runs down and focus verticals (EM-LAP and embedded finance) grow; focus share rose from 33% to 38% of AUM. Net total income grew 51% YoY and 34% QoQ, and PAT grew 26% YoY, after a one-time restructuring cost of about INR 25 crores. Management reiterated five FY29 commitments (85% focus-vertical AUM, INR 220 crore cost takeout, 15-20% annual Prime run-down, no new equity, ROA of 3-3.5%), and said FY27 is a transition year with only marginal ROA improvement. Q&A focused on growth outlook, co-lending exit, embedded-finance credit quality and the Profectus acquisition economics. Note: the call's Q4 net total income level and total PAT were not stated in the transcript.

financial_highlights.change: down 45 bps YoY; fifth consecutive quarterly improvement
one-time restructuring cost INR 25 crores (INR 25.4 crores per slide)

financial_highlights.value: INR 72 crores, 1.9% of average AUM annualised

financial_highlights.change: GNPA up from 2.2% QoQ, attributed to denominator effect

segments.name: Emerging Market LAP
segments.commentary: AUM INR 3,581 crores in Q4 with GNPA 1.2%; 317-318 branches across 13 states (up from 127 in FY24); vintage branches (>12 months) at INR 68 lakh/month disbursement vs ~INR 80 lakh target, with ~156 sub-six-month branches queued.

segments.name: Embedded finance (MyShubhLife)
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,280 crores, up 27% QoQ and 6x in 15 months; GNPA 1.7%; ~2.5 lakh active merchants; yields 24-26%; average ticket ~INR 1 lakh, daily EMI, one-year tenor.

segments.name: Prime intermediated (DSA-led, run-down)
segments.commentary: Being run down at 15-20% annually; co-lending and DA income INR 155 crores in Q4 (about 25% of total income), expected to taper from FY28. Profectus school financing book (~13% yield) being replaced by smaller Tier 2-4 school loans at 16-17%.

segments.name: Secured book overall
segments.commentary: Secured portfolio including machinery loans about 67% of total AUM with GNPA ~1.5%; unsecured (embedded plus business loans) capped at 30-35% of portfolio per management.

guidance_outlook: Combined opex (UGRO plus Profectus) to fall from ~INR 750 crores to INR 490-500 crores in FY27, described as a one-time takeout of ~INR 220 crores with no further opex increases.
AUM expected flattish in FY27 with uptick thereafter; focus verticals growing ~25% CAGR while the Prime book runs down 15-20% annually.
FY27 is a transition year with marginally better ROA than FY26; step-up expected in FY28-FY29, targeting ROA of 3-3.5% by FY29.
Credit cost expected in the zone of just under 2%, not more.
Cost of borrowing to keep improving; each 25 bps reduction worth INR 35-40 crores annualised; more ECBs planned, which land at ~9.5-10% INR-equivalent after hedging.
No incremental equity required through FY29; growth funded by internal accruals. Internal assessment points to a likely credit rating upgrade next year (A+ outlook positive).
capex_capacity: EM-LAP network at 317-318 branches across 13 states; no new branch investment planned, with focus on productivity per branch (target INR 60-70 lakh per month per branch in FY27 per management).
Profectus overlap: present in about 28 locations; one branch retained per location, with some Profectus and some UGRO branches vacated.
Infrastructure build-out for EM-LAP complete; all opex for branch expansion already incurred over the last two-three years.
Profectus acquisition: paid ~INR 1,400 crores cash for ~INR 1,200 crores net worth company; management expects ~INR 150 crores profit in year one.
demand_pricing: EM-LAP targets micro-SMEs with turnover under INR 3 crores (median ~INR 1 crore), secured loans of INR 7.5-50 lakh in Tier 2-4 towns; prior intermediated Prime LAP yielded ~13-15% and business loans ~18-19%, versus ~26% on embedded.
Management expects yields to face downward pressure over time, especially in intermediated Prime; sees EM-LAP as less exposed due to a fragmented market and branch-network differentiation.

Co-lending exit rationale: bank-linked co-lending assets are lower-yielding; management cites a 1% margin example after cost of borrowing and credit cost. Co-lending will continue but shrink as a share of income.
Embedded-finance GNPA at 1.7% vs 4-4.5% projected at product design; 6 cohorts have completed lifecycle. Credit cost for embedded about 1.5-1.6%, roughly 70-80% of GNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit the intermediated book, which was ~70% of AUM, and why stop co-lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower-yield DSA book lacked pricing advantage given cost of borrowing did not fall as expected; co-lending income is volatile and does not accrete to net worth; co-lending will continue but shrink. Secured EM-LAP has credit cost in the same band despite higher GNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Will AUM grow? Growth is slowing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 AUM is flattish with a pickup after; focus verticals grow ~25% CAGR (INR ~3,500 crores and ~INR 2,000 crores segments) while ~INR 10,000 crores runs down. Priority is bottom-line over scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Profectus given the planned shift to higher yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Profectus (INR ~180 crore cost base) was used to rationalise opex; the acquired portfolio generates cash profit that supports the new branch network, and the deal is ROE-accretive by ~10%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of rising NPAs and credit cost given flat AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cost will stay below ~2%. Repossessed asset resolution takes 12-15 months; 40-50% of cases settle after court order; recovery cost ~1%, with no principal loss so far.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex fall and how does the Profectus branch rationalisation flow through?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined opex falls to INR 490-500 crores from INR 750 crores; the INR 25 crore one-time cost has been fully provided this quarter, so savings should flow from Q1 and more from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fully diluted share count and are there remaining CCDs or warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total outstanding shares are 15.29 crore on a fully diluted basis, with 2 lakh shares pending conversion; all CCDs and warrants are matured or converted.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise ECBs when domestic borrowing is available, and is there an RBI limit?
qa_highlights.answer: No RBI cap on amount; ECBs are fully hedged and land at ~9.5-10%; DFIs are main lenders; more ECBs planned for cost and ALM benefits, with hedging cost currently higher.

risks_watch: Growth stalling: AUM flat in FY27; focus verticals must grow ~25% to offset the Prime run-down; GNPA may rise through denominator effect.
Embedded finance seasoning: management's 4-4.5% projected GNPA ceiling is well above current 1.7%, but only six cohorts have completed their lifecycle.
Yield compression in EM-LAP and embedded finance as competition emerges; management acknowledges downward pressure.
Execution of INR 490-500 crore opex target and whether savings flow from Q1-Q2 FY27 given notice-period costs.
Track the five FY29 commitments quarterly: focus share (38% now vs 85% target), opex ceiling, Prime run-down rate, no equity, ROA trajectory, and co-lending/DA income share (~25% of income now).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic pivot and cost takeout, with detailed numerical answers on the five commitments. Defensive when challenged on growth and co-lending exit, with management repeatedly reframing the story around bottom-line over scale.
key_quotes: After one full quarter of execution, all five are on track.
AUM is broadly flat quarter -on-quarter. That is intentional.
So total outstanding share should be INR 15.29 crores, yes.
So, the tracking number is that that we should not breach total cost of around INR 490 crores or INR 500 odd crores because we have said very clearly that our opex journey is over.
For the first time since UGRO's start, this company is now generating capital, not consuming it.
And currently, Rishi, the hedge cost has gone up. So that's why we are holding on to more ECB.

adds.what: EM-LAP branch network at 317-318 branches; no new branch investment planned, focus on productivity

growth.why: Management guides FY27 as a transition year with flattish AUM and only marginally better ROA, with opex falling to INR 490-500 crore backed by a cost takeout already under way, while the Prime book runs down 15-20% a year and focus verticals grow ~25% CAGR; no new capacity is planned and no revenue growth figure is guided.
